title: Animal Groups
subtitle: Grade 3 Science
objectives: Identify the distinguishing features of different groups of animals, including fish, reptiles, mammals, birds, amphibians and insects.
Use observations and tests to sort, group and classify objects.
Use secondary information sources to research an answer to a question.
Know that there are different types of models in science, including diagrams and physical models that we can touch.

beats.say: Look at an animal. What has it got? Scales, feathers, fur?
Those are features, and features put every animal into a group.
Scientists sort animals into six groups, by their features.
A feature is something the animal has: scales, feathers, fur, six legs.
Not where it lives. Not how it moves. Look at the animal itself.
Fish have scales and fins, and they breathe through gills.
A fish lives in water all its life. A salmon. A shark.
Amphibians have smooth, damp skin, with no scales at all.
They start life in water, as tadpoles. Frogs, toads and newts.
When they are grown, they come onto land as well.
Reptiles have dry, scaly skin. Snakes, lizards and tortoises.
Most reptiles lay tough eggs on land, not in water.
Birds have feathers and a beak, and they lay eggs.
Every bird has feathers, even a penguin that cannot fly.
Mammals have fur or hair, and they feed their babies milk.
Dogs, whales and bats are mammals. So are you.
Insects have six legs. Count them: always six.
An insect's body is in three parts: head, thorax and abdomen.
Ants, bees and beetles are insects. A spider has eight legs, so it is not.
Now sort. Ask about the skin, the legs, and how it feeds its young.
A whale lives in the sea, but it feeds its calf milk. A mammal.
A penguin swims, and it has feathers. That makes it a bird.
A bat flies, and it has fur and milk. A mammal that flies.
Some groups are easy to mix up. Then you look it up.
A fact card is a secondary source: what somebody else wrote down.
A crocodile lives in rivers, but it has dry scales. A reptile.
A diagram is a drawing with labels that name the parts.
It is one kind of model in science. You will label a beetle.
The head has the eyes and the mouth.
The thorax is the middle part, not the whole body. Six legs join there.
The abdomen is the back part, where the food goes.
Two antennae for feeling and smelling, and wings on the thorax.
Fish breathe with gills. Amphibians have smooth, damp skin.
Reptiles have dry scales. Birds have feathers and a beak.
Mammals feed their babies milk. Insects have six legs.
Sort by the features. Look up the tricky ones, and label your diagram.
